profile.headline: Software Developer
profile.summary:
Programmer, development manager

Co-founder of one of the first successful ebook companies. Development executive for Lotus Notes and other major software products.

Consultant on digital rights management and other aspects of online digital media.

Former social studies teacher in the Boston public schools.

Elected school committee member 2004–2007 and 2007–2010.  Elected town meeting representative in Lexington, Massachusetts 1997–2015 and 2022–present.

Exhibiting artist at the Cambridge Art Association and other U.S. galleries.

Specialties: Digital books. Education. Professional project management. Collaboration software. Computer security. US and world history. Photography.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
OpenEye Scientific is now the Molecular Sciences Division of Cadence.

I develop and extend and maintain the Sphinx system and other elements of the documentation infrastructure.

positions.title: Software Application Specialist
positions.description: Database programming, system analysis, and other software problem solving for the city's departments.  Develop and advise on RFPs for the city, providing technical review.

positions.title: Social studies teacher
positions.description: Fulfilling a long-time ambition and commitment, I taught ancient civilizations, geography, civics, and photography at the Boston Middle School Academy, a part of the Boston public school system.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: Consultant to the LOC's National Library Service for the Blind and Physically Handicapped, who are developing digital versions of their talking books for the blind and disabled citizens of the USA.  With NLS and other members of the DAISY consortium, developed system for copyright security.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: Consulted on design of digital rights management systems.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: Consulted to business development staff of this startup company from Cambridge, Massachusetts, developers of advanced public key certification technology.

positions.title: Senior Engineering Manager
positions.description: Managed Boston-area department of Acrobat engineering group, after my company's acquisition. Built eBook software into Adobe Reader. We also developed versions of the Glassbook-type Adobe ebook reader for handheld devices including Palm Pilots, Windows CE handhelds, and cellular phones. Developed digital rights management client and server technology.  Group consisted of about 15 people.

positions.title: Vice President of Product Development
positions.description: Co-founder of this developer of electronic book technology.  The Glassbook Reader was the first commercially successful ebook software reader--like the Kindle Reader I use today on my Mac and iPhone except that the year was 1999. We were the preferred technology for distribution of the most famous ebook of the founding era, Stephen King's novella Riding the Bullet. First products were built using PDF file format, and the company was acquired by Adobe Systems in 2000. Principal competitors were Nuvomedia (Gemstar), Peanut Press (Palm Digital Media), and Microsoft.

positions.title: Vice President of Product Development
positions.description: Project management for Lotus Notes engineering, a development organization that grew to about 450 technical people.  Iris was acquired by its marketing partner Lotus Development in 1994.  Lotus was acquired by IBM in 1995.  Notes was sold, in recent years, to HCL Technologies.

positions.title: Director of Engineering
positions.description: Led Cambridge-based engineering group of Security Dynamics.  Designed and developed client/server two-factor authentication product employing the company's primary invention, the SecurID card.  Security Dynamics went public in 1992 and later acquired RSA Data Security, changing its name to RSA Security. RSA was acquired in more recent years by EMC and after that by Dell Technologies.

positions.title: Director of Engineering
positions.description: Hired as documentation manager, became engineering director in 1985, responsible for development of the Genera operating system.  Led Software Products group: about 105 people in engineering, QA, documentation, software support, and training. Major projects included new OS versions for gate-array and single-board versions of the Symbolics Lisp Machine as well as the major feature release, Genera 7.0.

positions.title: Technical writer
positions.description: In 1977–1978, I was part of a small team of writers for the MINC, an innovative microcomputer system for scientific laboratories.  The documentation for MINC won the international first place prize from the Society for Technical Communication.  From 1978 to 1984, I worked for Dave Cutler's team, first on PL/I and C compiler projects for VAX/VMS and then on VAXELN, a new real-time operating system for the VAX.

positions.title: Technical writer
positions.description: This division of Logicon did large projects for the government, many but not all classified.  The largest project I worked on was the "bulk mail center" project for the US Postal Service, which sorted (and maybe still sorts) parcel post mail in huge factories.  The factories were newly built at the time, and the idea was to ensure a package could get between any two points in the USA in two days.

positions.title: Technical editor
positions.description: Edited online material for the Population Information Program.  It provided online abstracts of birth control information for health care professionals throughout the world.

positions.title: Technical editor
positions.description: Technical editor of the Journal of Comparative and Physiological Psychology.
